title: Surgical Smoke Removal in Laparoscopic Video
text:
Approach
Designed and implemented a full evaluation protocol — PSNR and SSIM on held-out validation data — benchmarked against published dehazing baselines, to test whether a model trained on a visually similar but physically different problem (outdoor haze vs. surgical smoke) generalizes without retraining.

title: Surgical Smoke Removal in Laparoscopic Video
text:
Implications
The results point to two concrete next steps for improving robustness in surgical desmoking: increasing architecture capacity and using density-aware training strategies, rather than assuming a haze-removal model transfers as-is.

title: Materials Science Toolbox
text: A general-purpose materials science toolbox built around a shared architecture: a common app shell that launches individual tools as standalone subprocesses, rather than one monolithic application. This keeps each tool independently launchable and lets different tools use different GUI frameworks if needed, while a shared core Python library (separate from any tool’s GUI) provides the underlying materials science logic every tool draws from.

title: Materials Science Toolbox
text:
Architecture

Shell architecture — a common launcher that starts each tool as its own subprocess, rather than routing everything through one internal application
Shared core library — materials science logic (phase diagrams, crystal structures, mechanical property estimation) lives separately from any individual tool’s GUI, so future tools can reuse it directly
Mechanical property estimation — currently Level 1 (equilibrium-only, phase-fraction-weighted estimates), with Level 3 (real kinetics — TTT/CCT diagrams, heat treatment effects) planned as a future addition

title: Predictive Maintenance: Unsupervised Failure Detection on Industrial Sensor Data
text:
An end-to-end predictive maintenance pipeline that detects equipment failure using unsupervised anomaly detection on multivariate sensor data — no labeled failure examples used during training, only clean “normal operation” data. The project covers the full lifecycle: raw sensor data → feature engineering → model validation → rigorous methodology debugging → feature selection experiments → a live historical-replay dashboard.
Stack: Python, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest), pandas, Jupyter, Plotly/ipywidgets for the live dashboard.

title: Predictive Maintenance: Unsupervised Failure Detection on Industrial Sensor Data
text:
Problem
Given a stream of ~40 sensor readings from an industrial pump system, predict impending failure early enough to act on it — using only examples of normal operation, since real failures are rare and expensive to label. The model needs to generalize across time: trained on the past, evaluated on the future, the way it would actually be deployed.

title: Predictive Maintenance: Unsupervised Failure Detection on Industrial Sensor Data
text:
Approach

Isolation Forest, trained exclusively on clean-baseline (normal) operation, flags future readings that don’t resemble it.
Walk-forward validation — chronological train/test splits, never trained on future data relative to what it’s evaluated against.
Engineered feature families: raw sensor readings (“core”), rolling mechanical features (velocity, amplitude, accumulated stress), and spectral features (FFT energy, dominant frequency, spectral entropy) — each tested standalone and in combination.

title: Predictive Maintenance: Unsupervised Failure Detection on Industrial Sensor Data
text:
Methodology highlights
This project’s real emphasis is rigor over headline numbers — several rounds of discovering and correcting subtle methodology issues that would have otherwise produced misleading results:

Found and fixed a feature-selection bias: an AUC-based ranking was unintentionally selecting features that separated post-failure recovery behavior rather than failure behavior itself — features with near-perfect individual separation scores that produced a near-useless model once combined. Diagnosed by breaking AUC down per machine-state pair rather than trusting a single combined metric.
Found and fixed a feature-scale bug: an engineered “accumulated stress” feature was an unbounded rolling sum, sitting at a scale thousands of times larger than other features — silently dominating the model’s decision splits. Fixed by converting it to a scale-normalized rate.
Found and fixed a silent pipeline bug: a per-experiment contamination-rate tuning step had been computed but never actually wired into model training — every experiment was silently using a generic default. Confirmed via a direct before/after comparison once corrected.
Compared two feature-selection philosophies head-to-head: ranking features by individual statistical separation (AUC) vs. testing each feature’s actual marginal contribution to model performance (ablation). The ablation approach surfaced a real, validated precision/recall trade-off that the AUC approach never found.

title: Predictive Maintenance: Unsupervised Failure Detection on Industrial Sensor Data
text:
Results
The raw sensor readings (“core” features) turned out to be the strongest standalone predictor — engineered mechanical and spectral features did not reliably improve on this baseline, a genuine negative result reached only after four separate rounds of fixes and a second, independent feature-selection method, not an unexamined gap.

The two final candidates represent a genuine trade-off rather than one being strictly better: the ablation-selected set trades precision and a higher false-alarm rate for meaningfully earlier warning — about 8 additional days of lead time before failure. Which one is “correct” depends on the operational cost of a false alarm versus the value of earlier warning, a business question the model itself can’t answer.
